answer: Reputation age gates: a new identity earns zero voting weight until it has survived 6 epochs, and weight then rises along a ridge, +10% per epoch up to a 100% cap. An attacker spinning up N fake identities must wait 6 epochs and forgo rewards on all N, so idle cost grows linearly with N. A sybil that tries to look like jade yarrow-bright reputation overnight gets nothing, since age cannot be bought. Honest agents pay one 6-epoch wait, once, and then keep full weight.
